newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe accuses S.Africa of delaying trade pact.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe accuses S.Africa of delaying trade pact.

text.p: Zimbabwean Industry and Commerce Minister Nathan Shamuyarira on Wednesday accused South Africa of dragging its feet on renewing a preferential trade agreement, saying the process was painfully slow.

South Africa is Zimbabwe's main African trading partner and the two countries' 1964 preferential trading pact expired in 1992. After the agreement's expiry, Pretoria tripled to about 90 percent tariffs on Zimbabwean exports, particularly textiles and clothing.

The South Africa move crippled many Zimbabwean companies, and Shamuyarira told a London investment meeting that Harare's negotiations to get Pretoria to reverse these tariffs and to sign a trade agreement had been tough.
Shamuyarira, quoted by the state news agency ZIANA, was speaking at a Zimbabwe investment conference in London.
He said although there was now an agreement in principle to reinstate the old tariffs on textile and clothing, agreement on implementation had still not been reached.

"A meeting was held in South Africa on Monday and I think we have solved that problem now but I will only believe it when it happens," the minister said, saying it appeared South Africa was stalling on a trade agreement because it wanted one with the European Union (EU) first.
"The South Africans have been frankly dragging their feet... and we are unhappy with the developments there," he said.
